member.name: T:Universal.Common.Css.Selectors.SelectorParser
member.summary: Parses CSS selector strings into structured selector objects according to CSS Selectors Level 4 specification. Supports complex selectors, pseudo-classes, pseudo-elements, attribute selectors, and functional selectors.

remarks.para: The SelectorParser handles the complete CSS selector syntax including:

item.description: Basic selectors (type, class, ID, universal, attribute)
Combinator selectors (descendant, child, adjacent sibling, general sibling)
Pseudo-class selectors (structural, user action, form state)
Complex selector lists with comma separation

remarks.para: The parser validates selector syntax and throws for invalid selectors. It follows the CSS specification for selector precedence and structural validation.

member.name: M:Universal.Common.Css.Selectors.SelectorParser.Parse(System.String)
member.summary: Parses a CSS selector string into a structured object.
member.param: The CSS selector string to parse. Can contain multiple selectors separated by commas. Examples: "div", ".class", "#id", "nav > ul li:hover", "h1, h2, h3"
member.returns: A containing the parsed selectors. Each selector in the list represents one complete selector (separated by commas in the input).
member.exception:
Thrown when the selector string contains invalid syntax, such as:
Invalid CSS identifiers
Malformed pseudo-class or pseudo-element syntax
Invalid combinator usage (e.g., starting or ending with a combinator)
Unbalanced parentheses or brackets
Invalid An+B expressions in structural pseudo-classes
Empty selectors or selector components

remarks.para: The method tokenizes the input string first, then parses the tokens into a selector structure. Invalid selectors within a comma-separated list are ignored, and only valid selectors are included in the result. If no valid selectors can be parsed, a is thrown.
The parser supports CSS Selectors Level 4 features including logical combinators (:is, :where, :not), the relational pseudo-class (:has), and advanced structural selectors with "of selector" syntax.
